title: Amazon (AMZN) is buying billions in Nvidia (NVDA) AI systems it can't yet turn on, Business Insider reports - Newsquawk
content: Deliveries of this kind, hardware arriving ahead of the power and cooling capacity needed to run it, have been a recurring feature of the AI buildout cycle, and the distinction that matters is between a supply bottleneck and a deployment bottleneck: the former constrains the chipmaker, the latter the hyperscaler, and the market has historically read them differently. For NVDA, racks shipped into staging count as recognized revenue at the point of delivery, so a buyer sitting on unpowered inventory flatters near-term shipments while raising the question of how much backlog is real end-demand versus capacity parked ahead of energization. For AMZN, the read runs through capex versus utilization: prior episodes where cloud operators absorbed hardware faster than facilities could be commissioned have eventually shown up as depreciation running ahead of AWS revenue, a gap the equity has historically punished when disclosed. The figures here come from internal correspondence cited by a single outlet, so confirmation sits with the next quarterly prints on both sides, specifically NVDA's shipments commentary and AMZN's capex and cloud capacity language. Worth noting that staged delivery before final deployment is also standard practice for large data center programs, so the telling detail is the scale relative to energization timelines rather than the existence of the staging itself. title: Nvidia Raises Stakes With Massive New AI Investment - TradingView
content: Nvidia NVDA is expanding its European AI footprint, announcing plans to back four German startups as part of a broader commitment of nearly $10 billion across companies, universities and research institutions in the region. The chipmaker said it will support Agile Robots, Avelios Medical, Mirelo and Reflex Aerospace, though it did not disclose how much it plans to invest in each company. The announcement came at the Invest in Germany Summit in Berlin, where Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang argued that artificial intelligence should be viewed as a productivity tool rather than a replacement for human capability. AI can only augment your capability; it will not replace your capability, Huang told attendees. The move shows Nvidia is trying to embed itself more deeply into Europe's emerging AI ecosystem. The company is also expanding its cooperation with the German federal government and the country's Industry 4.0 Platform, which brings together government, companies, researchers and trade groups to accelerate industrial AI adoption. That industrial angle may be particularly important. Siemens separately unveiled new AI tools built with Nvidia technology at its Erlangen factory. The company said the systems could reduce the engineering work required to prepare production by as much as 85%, while AI-driven production planning could cut costs by up to 20%. I think the bigger story here is that Nvidia is increasingly using capital and partnerships to create demand around its own technology. Backing startups, working with governments and integrating its platform into factories can make Nvidia more than a supplier of GPUs. It can help the company shape the broader AI infrastructure stack around its hardware and software ecosystem. That matters as Europe tries to build more domestic AI capacity and reduce dependence on technology developed elsewhere. For investors, the key things to watch are how much of Nvidia's European commitment turns into direct equity investments, whether industrial AI adoption accelerates, and how quickly projects such as the Siemens partnership translate into measurable productivity gains. Nvidia's European strategy increasingly looks less like a simple sales expansion and more like an effort to build the market around itself. Select market data provided by ICE Data Services. Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) has been one of the biggest winners of the artificial intelligence (AI) boom. But even its shareholders have reason to feel nervous. On Oct. 16, the Nasdaq Composite fell 2.2%, while the S&P 500 declined 1.2%. Technology stocks came under pressure as investors worried about rising borrowing costs and the debt piling up behind the AI infrastructure boom. Nvidia's shares also faced pressure, although the company remains highly profitable. Should existing shareholders sell before a potential market crash? Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue » I wouldn't sell Nvidia simply because the market looks shaky. I'd focus on three things: the health of its business, the size of my position, and my ability to withstand a sharp decline. Here's why. Nvidia's latest results show why investors remain excited about its future. In its second quarter of fiscal 2027, revenue surged 106% year over year to $96.2 billion. Data Center revenue, driven by demand for AI computing infrastructure, jumped 117% to $89 billion. Management expects revenue to reach $108 billion in the following quarter. These aren't just impressive numbers. They show that Nvidia is turning AI demand into enormous sales and profits. Its graphics processing unit (GPU) chips, networking products, and software help power the infrastructure that supports modern AI. While competitors are trying to catch up, Nvidia benefits from an established software ecosystem and close relationships with major customers. Still, that doesn't mean its lead is unassailable. Customers could reduce spending, competitors could gain ground, or growth could slow. But investors should distinguish between a temporary market sell-off and a deterioration in Nvidia's business. For instance, if its competitive advantages remain strong and earnings continue growing, a falling share price alone isn't a compelling reason to sell. Even a great company can become a risky investment if it takes up too much of your portfolio. Suppose Nvidia accounts for 40% of your investments. If its shares fall 50%, your total portfolio loses 20% of its value, assuming everything else stays unchanged. Could you tolerate that loss without panicking? If Nvidia has become an outsize position, trimming some shares may be sensible even if you remain optimistic about its future. You can reduce your risk without abandoning a company you believe will benefit from AI adoption. However, don't sell everything simply because you fear a crash. If you think Nvidia's business remains healthy and your position is manageable, holding through volatility may be reasonable. The goal isn't to avoid every decline. It's to avoid taking so much risk that a downturn forces you to make a decision you'll regret. Nobody knows whether the recent market weakness will develop into a full-blown crash. So, rather than trying to forecast the next move, prepare for different outcomes. First, maintain an emergency fund and avoid investing money you'll need for near-term expenses. You don't want an unexpected bill to force you to sell Nvidia at a depressed price. Second, examine your other holdings. If several depend on the same AI spending boom, your portfolio may be less diversified than you think. Finally, decide what price would make Nvidia attractive enough to buy more. Consider its future earnings, competitive advantages, and the risks to its growth. Don't assume a lower share price automatically makes it a bargain. If Nvidia becomes cheaper while its business remains strong, you may have an opportunity to gradually add shares. Nvidia remains a major beneficiary of AI infrastructure spending, but no stock is immune to market volatility or valuation risk. And since every investor is different -- with different time horizons, risk tolerances, and circles of competence -- it is impossible to offer a universal course of action. Instead, here's a good framework that investors can use to aid their decision: I'd hold if I think the business prospects remain strong in the coming quarters, the potential return is attractive, and my position is manageable. I'd trim if Nvidia has become too large a part of my portfolio. Finally, I'd reassess or sell if its competitive position weakens or its future returns no longer justify the risk. The key is to distinguish between market fear and business risk. Don't sell Nvidia simply because you're afraid of a crash. Just make sure you own an amount you can comfortably hold through one. Morgan Stanley expects spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure to reach $1.58 trillion in 2027, with Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) positioned to capture a substantial share of investment in computing equipment and data centers. The bank estimates that 91.7% of Nvidia’s projected 2027 revenue is exposed to AI infrastructure demand, the highest proportion among companies covered in its October 15 research report. Vertiv follows at 90%, while Broadcom has estimated exposure of 81%. Despite Nvidia’s concentration in AI infrastructure, Morgan Stanley identifies the semiconductor manufacturer as offering the most attractive risk-adjusted return among companies in the sector. The report, “Following AI’s $1.6 Trillion Money Trail: Mapping the Revenue Generated by the Capex Boom,” was prepared by Morgan Stanley’s North America Insight team, led by Nicholas Lentini. Its forecasts indicate substantial growth in AI infrastructure expenditure, alongside increasing dependence on debt financing, electricity availability and a relatively small group of major technology customers. Morgan Stanley estimates that hyperscalers and specialized AI cloud providers will spend approximately $980 bn in 2026, rising nearly 60% to $1.58 trillion in 2027 and reaching $1.8 trillion in 2028. The 2027 projection includes approximately $195 bn in data center leases, which Morgan Stanley categorizes as “synthetic capex” because these commitments do not appear as conventional capital expenditures in cash flow statements. Hyperscalers have disclosed more than $1.1 trillion in lease commitments that have yet to commence. According to the bank’s estimates, approximately $1 trillion of projected 2027 infrastructure spending will translate into revenue for S&P 500 companies, with nearly $700 bn attributed to Nvidia. Morgan Stanley calculates that revenue generated from hyperscaler and neocloud customers will represent approximately 5% of total S&P 500 revenue in 2027 while accounting for roughly 25% of the index’s revenue growth. The bank expects AI infrastructure investment to generate returns on invested capital of 25% to 50%. Its assessment also draws on four previous computing investment cycles: personal computers, the internet, mobile computing and cloud infrastructure. Across those cycles, Morgan Stanley estimates that Wall Street underestimated the scale of computing investment by an average of 38%. Morgan Stanley’s forecasts show substantial concentration within Nvidia’s customer base. In the bank’s 2027 model, SpaceX and Amazon Web Services account for approximately 54% of Nvidia’s hyperscaler revenue and 72% of its projected growth in that customer segment. These figures illustrate Nvidia’s dependence on investment decisions made by a small number of large infrastructure operators. Morgan Stanley considers its revenue assumptions for SpaceX and Amazon conservative. The bank’s model projects that Nvidia’s share of spending by other major hyperscalers will decline from 18% in 2026 to 16% in 2027, although Nvidia expects to increase its market share. The company’s data center business already accounts for most of its sales, making continued investment in AI computing capacity central to its earnings outlook. Morgan Stanley’s global investment committee acknowledged this dependence in March, identifying the durability of AI capital expenditure as a primary condition supporting the technology-led equity market advance. Nvidia’s latest financial results demonstrate the scale of demand for its computing products. The company reported revenue of $96.22 bn for the second quarter of fiscal 2027, ended July 26, 2026, an increase of 105.8% from a year earlier. Data Center revenue reached $89.02 bn, up 117% year over year. Net income increased 126% to approximately $59.69 bn, while adjusted earnings reached $2.22 per share, exceeding analysts’ expectations of approximately $2.09. Nvidia has exceeded consensus earnings-per-share estimates for six consecutive quarters. Chief Executive Jensen Huang described demand as accelerating during the company’s second-quarter earnings announcement. The company is expanding production of its Vera Rubin computing platform, which is expected to support the next phase of demand from hyperscalers and specialized AI cloud providers. The platform is also central to projections of continued revenue growth in fiscal 2028. Nvidia shares closed at $217.09 on October 19, 2026, up 1.38% for the session, giving the company a market capitalization of approximately $5.23 trillion. Despite substantial share-price appreciation in recent years, its earnings valuation has declined as profits have grown faster than its stock price. Nvidia trades at slightly more than 27 times trailing 12-month earnings, its lowest trailing P/E ratio since June 2019, according to YCharts. The company’s average trailing P/E over the past decade was approximately 61.3. Its current multiple is therefore less than half its ten-year average, although it remains above the S&P 500’s trailing P/E of approximately 24.9. Alphabet, Amazon and Meta Platforms also trade at lower trailing earnings multiples than Nvidia. Forward valuations present a different comparison. Based on projected fiscal 2028 earnings, Nvidia trades at approximately 14 to 15 times earnings, depending on the forecast used. That multiple is below the forward valuations of the other Magnificent Seven companies and compares with an estimated 21 to 23 times forward earnings for the S&P 500. The valuation reflects expectations for continued rapid earnings growth, but also depends on the accuracy of analysts’ fiscal 2028 forecasts. Consensus earnings estimates for Nvidia have increased substantially during the past three months. Analysts project fiscal 2028 earnings per share of approximately $15.91, compared with $12.71 estimated 90 days earlier. The latest projection represents approximately 71% growth from expected fiscal 2027 earnings of $9.31 per share. Over the past 30 days, analysts submitted 46 upward earnings revisions and no downward revisions, according to the estimates cited in the October 19 market analysis. The average analyst price target stands at $328.72, approximately 51% above Nvidia’s October 19 closing price of $217.09. Of 62 analysts included in the cited coverage, 59 have positive ratings, two recommend holding the shares and one has a sell recommendation. A separate valuation scenario published by 24/7 Wall St. examines the possibility of Nvidia reaching $400 per share in 2027. At $400, Nvidia would trade at approximately 25 times projected fiscal 2028 earnings of $15.91 per share. That valuation would require an increase of approximately 84% from the October 19 closing price, substantially exceeding the current average analyst target. The scenario depends on continued earnings growth, successful deployment of Vera Rubin products and sustained hyperscaler demand. It also assumes investors would assign Nvidia a higher multiple than its current fiscal 2028 forward valuation. Morgan Stanley expects 2027 to produce the largest cash flow deficit in its forecast period for major AI infrastructure customers, increasing their dependence on borrowing. Hyperscalers have issued approximately $255 bn in unsecured bonds during 2026, equivalent to roughly 30% of estimated capital spending. The bank modeled how additional borrowing could affect interest coverage ratios, which measure earnings available to service interest obligations. In its hypothetical scenario, the combined interest coverage ratio for Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Microsoft, all rated AA or higher, declines from approximately 31 times to 12 times. Morgan Stanley also identifies higher equipment prices as a contributor to infrastructure spending growth. Amazon’s finance chief attributed most of an increase in the company’s capital expenditure plan, from $200 bn to approximately $220 bn, to rising memory costs rather than an expansion of planned infrastructure capacity. That distinction affects forecasts of how much additional computing infrastructure higher spending will actually deliver. Electricity availability presents another limitation on AI infrastructure deployment. Morgan Stanley forecasts a US data center power shortfall of approximately 32 gigawatts through 2028, equivalent to roughly one-third of the 97 gigawatts required. The bank’s investment projections assume that purchased computing equipment can ultimately be connected to operating data centers. Power shortages could delay those installations even if hyperscalers continue ordering processors. Morgan Stanley warns that companies may accumulate graphics processing units before securing sufficient electricity, potentially leaving expensive equipment unused. Continued advance purchasing could sustain Nvidia’s near-term chip revenue while increasing inventory exposure for its customers. The bank also identifies potential regulatory restrictions on data center construction and the possible reduction of government tax incentives as risks to infrastructure investment. It does not expect a federal moratorium on data center development, but considers tax incentives a potential target for legislative changes. Morgan Stanley’s downside scenario focuses on the possibility that infrastructure spending stabilizes before suppliers have adjusted production capacity. In that environment, shipment volumes could remain relatively stable while equipment prices decline, reducing supplier profitability. The bank cites the NAND memory downturn in late 2022, when shipments fell approximately 5% but prices declined 20% to 30%. Morgan Stanley expects suppliers of memory, optical components and other relatively small parts to face greater disruption if orders weaken or customers accumulate excess inventory. Nvidia could be less exposed to the initial adjustment because of its position as the largest supplier of high-value computing equipment. Nevertheless, simultaneous declines in processor prices and shipment volumes would present a more substantial earnings risk. Nvidia also faces competition from AMD and internally developed AI processors at Amazon, Alphabet and Microsoft. Morgan Stanley argues that investors may be underestimating the potential scale of spending reductions if the AI infrastructure investment cycle weakens. The bank’s projections remain positive, but their realization depends on financing conditions, customer investment plans and the ability of infrastructure operators to deploy the computing equipment they purchase. For Nvidia, those assumptions are central to both Morgan Stanley’s projected 2027 revenue exposure of 91.7% and Wall Street’s expectations for fiscal 2028 earnings growth.

title: Nvidia Backs Four German AI Startups in Broader European Expansion - TradingView
content: Nvidia Corp. (NVDA, Financials), the AI chipmaker, is expanding its footprint in Europe with plans to invest in four German startups. The companies are Agile Robots, Avelios Medical, Mirelo and Reflex Aerospace. Nvidia did not disclose how much it plans to invest in each. The investments are part of a broader commitment of nearly $10 billion to European companies, universities and research institutions. That makes the strategy bigger than venture funding alone. Nvidia is also working more closely with Germany's federal government and the country's Industry 4.0 Platform to accelerate AI adoption across manufacturing and other industrial sectors. Siemens provided an early example of what that could look like. The company unveiled new Nvidia-powered AI tools at its Erlangen factory and said the technology could reduce engineering work needed to prepare production by as much as 85%. AI-driven production planning could also cut costs by up to 20%. The more European companies build AI into factories, robotics, health care and aerospace, the larger the addressable market becomes for its hardware and software ecosystem. title: NYSE American Options launches extended trading hours for SPY, NVDA and peers - InvestmentNews
content:
NYSE American Options has introduced pre- and post-market trading sessions for a select group of equity options, expanding access for advisors and their clients beyond the standard trading day. The New York Stock Exchange, part of Intercontinental Exchange, Inc. (NYSE: ICE), launched NYSE American Options Extended Trading Hours (ETH) on October 20, 2026, giving market participants additional access to options listed on NYSE American. The initial group of eligible symbols includes options overlying key macroeconomic-focused ETFs (SPY, IWM, and GLD) alongside options on large-cap technology names including Apple, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Alphabet, Amazon, and Oracle. The early trading session runs from 7:30 AM to 9:25 AM ET, while the late trading session operates from 4:00 PM to 4:15 PM ET. The launch positions NYSE American in a fast-moving race among major exchanges to extend options access. Cboe Global Markets received SEC approval in May 2026 to offer extended trading hours for select multi-listed equity options on the Cboe Options Exchange, with that offering beginning July 13, 2026. NYSE American said that investor demand to trade options outside regular hours was growing, that non-U.S. investors found it difficult to participate when options traded only during the standard U.S. session, and that U.S. investors trading stocks after hours could not access the options market to hedge their positions. For advisors using options strategies to manage client risk particularly around earnings events or macro data releases, the expanded window provides a longer runway to respond to overnight news before the core session opens. Extended hours trading will be limited to up to 100 multiply-listed equity option classes meeting specific eligibility criteria, including average daily options volume of 150,000 contracts, underlying equity market capitalization of $50 billion, and underlying equity average daily trading volume of 10 million shares. Kevin Tyrrell, Chief Product Officer at NYSE, said the move "reflects market demand for investment opportunities and reliable risk management during a longer period of time," adding that the exchange plans to bring a similar approach to equities in December 2026. Brokers are also required to disclose specific risks to clients before accepting orders for extended-hours execution. Required disclosures must cover material trading risks such as lower liquidity, higher volatility, changing prices, exaggerated effects from news announcements, and wider bid-ask spreads. The NYSE move also signals a broader structural shift in market infrastructure. Five symbols (GLD, IWM, QQQ, SPY, and XLF) already traded until 4:15 PM ET under existing rules, with this launch now formalizing and expanding those sessions alongside the new pre-market window. For more details on eligible symbols and session rules, the NYSE American Options Extended Trading Hours Fact Sheet is available via ICE's public documents portal. title: NVDA, MU, QCOM Stocks Hit 52-Week Highs Last Week: What's Behind The Surge? - Stocktwits
content: Nvidia (NVDA), Micron Technology (MU), and Qualcomm (QCOM) all hit 52-week highs on Friday, showing that investors are jointly rethinking and raising the value of major semiconductor companies. The move reflected a decisive shift in sentiment around artificial intelligence infrastructure, with investors increasingly focused on the scale and durability of global compute demand rather than early-stage AI speculation. Nvidia reached a new 52-week high of $217.80, pushing its valuation past $5.23 trillion. The company’s rally was fueled by rising expectations around its next-generation Vera Rubin computing platform, which is designed to support advanced AI systems capable of autonomous, multi-step task execution. Market participants are now viewing Nvidia less as a traditional chipmaker and more as a foundational provider of global AI infrastructure. Nvidia has invested more than $40 billion in company stakes this year, spreading its money across different parts of the AI industry. This includes about $30 billion in OpenAI and smaller investments in firms like Corning, IREN, and Marvell. The strategy shows Nvidia is building influence across the full AI system. Nvidia stock closed Friday over 1% higher. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock remained in ‘extremely bullish’ territory. On Friday, Micron stock jumped 15.4%, lifting its market value above $842 billion. The company’s rally was powered by strong demand across its high-bandwidth memory segment and next-generation storage products. Investors reacted positively to confirmation that Micron’s advanced HBM4 supply is already fully allocated through 2026. At the same time, the company’s new 245TB 6600 ION solid-state drive added another growth catalyst. The product is designed to increase storage efficiency in AI data centers, allowing operators to expand capacity without increases in power usage or physical infrastructure. Qualcomm stock joined the rally as optimism grew beyond data centers into everyday devices. Its growth in AI-powered PCs and mid-range phones shows AI is moving closer to users, not just the cloud. On Friday, Daiwa analyst Louis Miscioscia upgraded Qualcomm to ‘Outperform’ from ‘Neutral’ and raised his price target to $225 from $140. Miscioscia said that the adjustment followed a reassessment of Qualcomm’s long-term opportunity, particularly as its exposure to data-center AI processors is beginning to attract more investor focus despite mixed quarterly results. Qualcomm stock ended Friday over 8% higher. Retail sentiment around the stock remained in ‘bullish’ territory. So far this year, MU stock has surged by over 161%, while NVDA and QCOM have gained 15% and 28%, respectively. Cohen’s chart posted on X showed drops in active buyers, sales volume, and operating profit, while operating costs increased during the same period. “Only in corporate America,” he said, adding a poop emoji. The chart showed eBay’s active buyers fell from 165 million in 2020 to 135 million in 2025, an 18% drop. Its total gross merchandise volume (GMV) also declined from $87.6 billion to $79.6 billion. The post said eBay’s operating profit fell from $2.64 billion in 2020 to $2.28 billion in 2025, while expenses rose from $4.46 billion to $5.65 billion despite having fewer users. The image also shed light on CEO compensation, listing cumulative executive pay of $144 million over the period shown. GameStop is planning a $56 billion acquisition of eBay and expects to save $2 billion annually within a year of the deal's completion, with Cohen as CEO of the merged company. Last week, the “Big Short” investor Michael Burry, in his Substack post, questioned the logic behind the deal structure and warned of risks tied to heavy debt and shareholder dilution. “The debt level needed to get this deal done would likely take 7-10 years to pay down and even then only if all capital was directed to such a task,” said Burry. He further added that a compensation structure tied to market capitalization and earnings growth may encourage deal strategies that appear to expand valuation but, in actuality, increase dilution risk for shareholders. “Ryan is promising huge cost cuts and massive jumps in profitability. This also makes sense. It is the Wall Street playbook. If eBay doubles its EBIT margin of 20% to 40%, it would be on par with Meta and 50% better than Alphabet. But it would not get eBay to a spot where it could pay off the debt in a few years, as Ryan is promising, Burry said.” Though GameStop’s board has endorsed the proposal unanimously, eBay’s directors are still reviewing the offer. Memory chip stocks surged overnight heading into Monday, signaling renewed momentum in a sector that has continued to captivate investors, with retail traders increasingly betting Micron could eventually reach a $1 trillion market capitalization. Micron stock was up 4%, while SanDisk shares gained 2% and Western Digital Corp. shares gained 1%. Micron rallied 38% last week, its best week since December 2008, and was the second-highest gainer in the Nasdaq-100 index. In recent weeks, upbeat quarterly reports from chip giants Intel and Advanced Micro Devices, along with hyperscalers Alphabet, Microsoft, and Amazon, have reinforced that AI demand and data center buildouts remain on a sharp upward trajectory — a trend that bodes well for the memory chip sector. SanDisk gained 32%, and Western Digital rose 11% last week. The companies reported upbeat reports on April 30 and May 1, respectively; the stocks initially fell before rising sharply in the coming days. The Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM), which tracks memory stocks including those of overseas giants like SK Hynix and Samsung, rose 30%, its best week since the fund was launched on April 2. Last week, Micron announced that it had begun shipping its 245TB Micron 6600 ION SSD, the world's highest-capacity commercially available data center SSD. Targeted at AI, cloud, hyperscale, and enterprise workloads, it delivers major efficiency gains, requiring roughly 82% fewer racks and far less physical space and power than HDD-based alternatives. Despite the sharp gains, traders believe the momentum in these stocks is still in its early stages. “From 2013-2015, Micron was actually worth significantly more than Nvidia, but that was before Nvidia got into the data center business. As AI workloads become more memory and CPU intensive ($INTC $AMD), this ratio can easily get back to ~40% again where it was for so many years. There's a reason $MU and $SNDK have been bought up like crazy on even the slightest of dips all year long,” posted a trader on Stocktwits. Another wrote that memory stocks are “not even close to being overvalued with this new paradigm shift in non cyclical memory demand” and forecast Micron to soon reach $1,000, or 34% higher from its last close. “Micron $MU needs to hit approximately $886 to join the Trillion market cap club. It will be a monumental moment for the memory bulls after being called crazy for the past 10 months,” a trader said. Shares of AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) jumped 2% in overnight trading heading into Monday, ahead of its earnings report, after company executives highlighted rising U.S. government opportunities and rapid scaling at its massive new Texas satellite manufacturing facility. ASTS stock snapped three straight weeks of losses, ending 6% higher at $75.05. Michael P., who leads U.S. government strategy, business development and sales at AST SpaceMobile, noted on LinkedIn the company’s ability to manufacture at scale through its new Midland facility, along with its existing West Texas operations. “At AST SpaceMobile, our capacity to manufacture enormous satellites at scale and doing this with incredible speed, while demonstrating our flexibility to meet the warfighter needs have made us more important than ever to the USG community,” he said. Separately, Roy Sofer, AST SpaceMobile’s chief engineer and senior vice president of engineering, said on LinkedIn that the facility represents the “highest standard of space production at scale.” Last week, AST SpaceMobile released a promotional tour video of its new Midland, Texas manufacturing site, a 500,000-square-foot facility built for high-volume production of “Microns,” the modular building blocks used in the company’s next-gen BlueBird satellites. The new facility tour video highlighted AST SpaceMobile’s vertically integrated manufacturing strategy and its efforts to rapidly scale satellite production for its space-based cellular broadband network. The video showed robotic assembly systems, automated production lines, testing stations and technicians assembling satellites. AST SpaceMobile said that the Midland site can produce up to six satellites per month, backing one to two launches every one to two months on average. The next-gen BlueBird satellites are expected to carry some of the largest commercial phased-array systems deployed in low Earth orbit (LEO), enabling direct-to-cell broadband connectivity for standard, unmodified smartphones. The Midland expansion is also part of AST SpaceMobile’s manufacturing footprint, which spans facilities across Texas and Florida, with over 1,800 workers in Texas operations alone. Wall Street is now turning its attention to AST SpaceMobile’s first-quarter (Q1) earnings report due Monday. Fiscal AI estimates revenue of $40 million for the quarter, compared with $3.25 million a year earlier. Analysts also expect a narrower quarterly loss of $0.17 per share, compared with $0.21 per share last year. According to Koyfin data, analysts maintain an average 12-month price target of $83.9 on ASTS shares, implying a 12% upside from current levels. The manufacturing update comes after AST SpaceMobile said that three BlueBird satellites are scheduled for a mid-June launch aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket. The company also said that 32 next-generation satellites are already in advanced stages of assembly. The update eased some investor concerns that AST SpaceMobile’s deployment timeline had been derailed after last month’s failed BlueBird-7 mission aboard Blue Origin’s New Glenn Mission-3 launch. Last month, BlueBird-7 successfully separated from the rocket but failed to reach its intended orbit after the launch vehicle’s second stage malfunctioned. AST SpaceMobile previously said that the satellite is expected to de-orbit and that insurance is expected to cover the loss. The failed deployment triggered a sharp selloff in ASTS shares and intensified concerns around whether the company can still achieve its goal of placing 45 satellites into orbit by year-end. However, Bank of America Securities (BofA) has estimated that the company could fall short of that target by seven satellites. Investors are also monitoring recent stake sales from Rakuten Mobile, AST SpaceMobile’s largest investor. A recent filing showed that Rakuten completed its previously disclosed trading plan and sold all shares included under the program. According to the filing, Rakuten Mobile, founder Hiroshi Mikitani and Rakuten Group now collectively own 15.5 million ASTS shares, representing a 5.3% stake, down from 11% previously. The filing detailed several open-market sales between April 27 and May 5, including a 1.8 million-share sale on April 30. Final transactions were executed at average prices of $65 per share. Shares of MoonLake Immunotherapeutics, Inc. (MLTX) jumped 7% in overnight trading heading into Monday after the company said that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) aligned on its approval filing plans for Sonelokimab, prompting Clear Street to say that the skin therapy could emerge with a “stronger, best-in-class label.” MLTX stock snapped two straight weeks of weekly losses and ended 2% higher last week at $17.06. On Sunday, MoonLake said that its final pre-biologics license application (BLA) meeting with the FDA concluded with alignment on certain parts of its application for Sonelokimab in hidradenitis suppurativa (HS), a chronic inflammatory skin disease. MoonLake said that the FDA agreed the results from both its mid-stage Mira study and late-stage Vela trials can be included in the proposed prescribing label for Sonelokimab, boosting the drug’s case for approval in HS. The company also said that the FDA supported including data from the Vela-Teen study, which could allow the treatment to be approved for patients aged 12 and older. The company plans to apply for a Priority Review designation and expects to submit the BLA application by September. Acceptance of the filing, including a decision on Priority Review status, is expected by November. MoonLake also said that the FDA identified no remaining gaps, including manufacturing-related issues, that would prevent the filing. MoonLake said that the proposed label could highlight that 43% of patients in the Mira study achieved a high level of symptom improvement after 12 weeks of treatment, with results outperforming placebo by 29 percentage points. According to the company, the efficacy levels are the strongest reported so far in any well-controlled late-stage clinical study for HS. After the FDA meeting, Clear Street said that MoonLake’s positive pre-application meeting restores the company to its “prior strong positioning” in the HS market. The brokerage said that the FDA’s agreement to include both Mira efficacy data and Vela trial results in the label could result in a “stronger, best-in-class label” for Sonelokimab. Clear Street maintained a ‘Buy’ rating on the stock with a $70 price target, implying  an upside of 310% from current levels. As of March 31, MoonLake held $357.9 million in cash, cash equivalents and short-term marketable securities, which it expects to fund operations and spending through the end of 2027. The company also retains access to up to $400 million in additional non-dilutive funding through its Hercules Capital debt facility. Research and development expenses totaled $54.5 million during the first quarter, compared with $56 million in the previous quarter. General and administrative expenses rose to $15.5 million from $9.2 million in the prior quarter. MoonLake said the increase was mainly from $4.8 million in accelerated expense recognition related to the voluntary cancellation of unvested stock option awards. The FDA update comes on the heels of encouraging long-term clinical data reported by MoonLake from the Phase 3 Vela-1 and Vela-2 trials in HS. In March, the company said 62% of patients treated with Sonelokimab achieved strong clinical improvement after 40 weeks, while up to 32% saw their skin lesions become nearly clear. Up to 25% of patients achieved inflammatory remission, meaning that the key signs of the disease disappeared completely. Patients also reported improvements in pain, mobility and daily activities such as walking and dressing. According to the company, up to 43% of patients saw reductions in their worst skin pain, while 65% reported improvements in overall quality of life. Earlier this year, MoonLake reported positive mid-stage trial results for Sonelokimab in axial spondyloarthritis, an inflammatory condition that affects the spine and joints. The company said that 81% of patients showed improvement within 12 weeks of treatment, with scans and disease markers also indicating reduced inflammation and disease activity. Investors are now watching several upcoming catalysts over the next year, including 52-week data from the Phase 3 Vela studies in the second quarter, results from the Phase 3 Izar-1 trial in psoriatic arthritis and data from the Vela-Teen adolescent study in mid-2026, followed by the BLA submission for HS by the end of September. Coinbase pays us for certain activity generated through this link. Prices displayed are informational. Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) is the market's most valuable company by market cap. It's the only one entering this week with a market cap north of $5 trillion. Instinctively, you might think that the priciest name among U.S.-listed companies would also be one of the most expensive names on Wall Street. Looking back, it's not entirely cheap. Nvidia trades for 27 times adjusted earnings on a trailing basis. It's not an outrageous price tag. It's also not bargain bin fodder. However, when you start to zoom out -- for a clear view of both the recent past and the next few years of projected growth -- the value in Nvidia stock starts to shine through. Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue » There's no point in burying the lede. Nvidia is currently trading for a modest 8 times what analysts see it earning in fiscal 2030. The key word there is "currently" since a profit target is a movable feast. It may be academically correct to say that you can buy Nvidia today at a 2030 P/E multiple of 8, but the chances of that actually being the case once we get there are slim. It could be considerably higher. It could be considerably lower. Projections will change, but let's lay out today's table. Here is what analysts see Nvidia generating in normalized earnings through the next few years, and the respective P/E ratio based on where the stock is now. Data source: S&P Global. Nvidia's fiscal year 2027 will end on Jan. 31, 2027. It's like a football kick in swirling winds. The longer you have to travel to get through the goalposts, the more variance there will be when the football gets there. So, yes, Nvidia is trading at 8 times what analysts expect it to earn on an adjusted basis in fiscal 2030. Don't bet on it landing there. Nvidia has been a spectacular investment. As the undisputed leader in artificial intelligence infrastructure, it's been feasting on the boom lately. Just check out the accelerating revenue growth that Nvidia has posted in the last few quarters. Making a great trend even better, the bottom line is growing even faster. It won't always be that way. Nvidia's own guidance suggests revenue will decelerate slightly in the current quarter, which ends next week. Bulls can rightfully counter that Nvidia has a long track record of exceeding its conservative guidance, but a slowdown is as natural as it is inevitable. The wonderful thing about momentum is that analysts' profit targets for future years have been rising with every blowout quarter. Wall Street pros weren't expecting Nvidia to earn $25.98 per share in fiscal 2030 a year ago, just as they weren't expecting a per-share profit of $9.31 this year. I want to close on one final point. Fiscal 2030 may seem like it's four years away. It's not. In fact, in a little more than three months, Nvidia will dip its toe into fiscal 2028. Fiscal 2030 starts just two years, three months, and less than two weeks from now. So Nvidia is already cheaper than you probably think. It's trading for just 13 times next year's earnings. Why do you think Nvidia's board recently authorized a record $150 billion in share repurchases? It's not the only one that thinks the stock is pretty cheap these days. This can all change, of course. Tailwinds can become headwinds. Growth can slow sharply instead of modestly. Nvidia's chunky net margins can contract. Every investor should have a long-term mindset paired with short-term vigilance. It's paid off so far, with Nvidia stock being a nine-bagger over the past five years. Don't be surprised if this winner keeps winning. NVDA’s stock fell as much as 5.3% amid broader weakness in the market and was among the top trending tickers on Stocktwits at the time of writing. According to a Bloomberg report, Nvidia committed $5 billion to Safe Superintelligence Inc. (SSI), marking one of the chipmaker's largest funding deals of the AI boom. Beyond the funding, SSI will also receive access to Nvidia's next-generation Vera Rubin AI platform, which the companies said could expand the startup's computing capacity by an order of magnitude. "We have research that is worthy of scaling up, and having access to a big NVIDIA computer will let us do so," SSI co-founder and chief executive Ilya Sutskever said. The reported SSI investment adds to Nvidia’s growing portfolio of AI startup investments, including bets across the broader AI stack such as OpenAI, Nebius (NBIS), CoreWeave (CRWV), IREN (IREN), and other companies building the infrastructure that powers large-scale model training and deployment. Many of these firms also rely on Nvidia’s chips, networking, and compute platforms. That strategy has increasingly drawn scrutiny from some market observers, including Michael Burry, who state that it creates a tightly interconnected ecosystem in which Nvidia finances companies that subsequently become major customers for its hardware. Monday's decline in Nvidia shares came amid renewed pressure across the semiconductor sector. According to The Information, China has begun producing domestically developed 193-nanometer immersion DUV lithography systems, with the first machines expected to ship this year to SMIC, Hua Hong, and CXMT. Meanwhile, memory manufacturer CXMT made its stock market debut, with shares reportedly surging more than fivefold, making it the most valuable newly listed company in mainland China. Retail traders, however, questioned whether Monday's semiconductor selloff was overdone. As Senate Republicans push toward a procedural vote on the CLARITY Act this week, New York Attorney General Letitia James is urging lawmakers to rethink the legislation. The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act (CLARITY Act) would limit the ability of state and local law enforcement to police crypto scams, James said in written testimony to the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee’s Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations on Monday. James testified that the CLARITY Act would shift oversight of digital assets to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) and preempt state regulation, hampering her office’s ability to pursue enforcement actions against crypto platforms. James called on Congress to increase federal oversight of cryptocurrency platforms. "My office has been leading the fight against cryptocurrency fraud," James testified. "Our rules-based market system gives people confidence that they can do business here. Without adequate laws and regulations, financial crises ensue. We urge Congress to safeguard our financial markets and protect America's investors, their future, our economy, and national security." The testimony said that complaints to the Office of the Attorney General (OAG) about cryptocurrency scams have tripled in the last three years. Reported scam losses have reached around $500 million over the past five years, while investors have lost billions more in crypto company bankruptcies. James called on Congress to enact legislation that would mandate crypto platforms to comply with anti-money laundering, know-your-customer and cybersecurity rules to prevent the funding of terrorism. The proposed framework would also ban untraceable crypto, including funds routed through mixers, from being converted to U.S. dollars, while keeping existing coverage of crypto under money transmission, commodities and securities law. James asked for platforms to identify anomalous trading activity and bad actors, and to hold them financially liable for fraud, along the lines of the Electronic Funds Transfer Act. James also called on Congress to ban elected officials and recent government employees from working in crypto regulation due to potential conflicts of interest and violations of the Emoluments Clause. Previously, Senator Cynthia Lummis (R-WY) addressed the concerns put forward by James, saying that passing the CLARITY Act would close the “DINO loophole,” short for Decentralized In Name Only, and make provisions for bad actors to stop any money laundering activity. The bill “brought every corner of the digital asset market inside the Bank Secrecy Act and sanctions framework,” Lummis said last week. James’ testimony lands as the Senate heads into its last two-week sprint before the August recess. Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-SD) is also reportedly planning to push for a procedural vote on the legislation this week, whether or not Democrats agree to a proposed deal on ethics restraints attached to the bill, as per PunchBowl News. “GOP leaders are hoping to run up the score on that procedural vote to make it easier to strike a deal, collapsing debate time and moving quickly to a final passage vote — possibly by week’s end,” said the report.
